Header:
Date: 2026-08-03
Time: 15:14 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jesse Kim (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Atlas Health - Platform Eng), Miguel Rivera (Atlas Health - SRE), Priya Sharma (Atlas Health - Security), Ethan Park (Atlas Health - CTO)

Optional summary (auto): Quick walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis and request logs. Discussed how to map traces to request logs, retention and RBAC, KMS/SOC2 questions, and a plan for a 1-day perf benchmark. Next steps include sandbox access, pricing/SOW, and compliance docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. we also have Jesse from our solutions engineering team. how's everybody doing?
[00:08] Laura: good thanks, excited to see the console walkthrough. we sent over a couple of failing request ids in chat.
[00:12] Jesse: awesome, we'll pull those in. quick agenda: console tracing, error analysis page, request logs, and debugging flows + questions. we'll show how to go from a trace to the raw request logs.
[00:22] Ethan: sounds good. our main goal today is to validate observability for production incidents and understand data residency / encryption constraints.
[00:30] Samir: great, and to add context, Atlas Health is looking at a Dedicated or Private deployment but wants to check hosted first for speed to value. so we'll touch on tradeoffs.
[00:40] Speaker 1: (mumbles)
[00:44] Jesse: ok i'm going to share my screen  tell me if the stream lags. first is the traces view in the Redwood Concole  typo there, console  so you'll see request traces aggregated by route and model version.
[00:55] [01:05] Jesse: here we have a sample trace that shows a spike in token generation latency around step 3, you can expand spans to see the model server time vs network time. note the span names are sometimes fuzzy depending on the model runtime  e.g., 'kv-cache-lookup' might appear as 'K V cash lookup' in our transcription export, which can confuse simple string matches.
[01:30] Laura: can you show how we jump from that trace to the raw request logs?
[01:34] Jesse: sure, every trace has a request_id at the top. clicking opens the trace detail on the right and there's a 'view request logs' link. that link filters the request logs by request_id and shows the full payload, headers (redacted if you set PII rules), and the response.
[01:50] Miguel: do logs show user input? we need to ensure PHI is not present in logs by default.
[01:55] Jesse: good question  by default we redact sensitive fields if you enable data-sanitization. for Hosted we provide configurable redaction rules; for Dedicated/Private you can enforce on your side or use our pipeline with customer-managed keys.
[02:10] Priya: speaking of keys, what's the KMS story? we need to know HSM/KMS for encryption at rest.
[02:15] Samir: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS with Dedicated and Private. Hosted can integrate with your cloud KMS for dedicated tenant keys; HSM integrations are on the roadmap  we can share the KMS integration doc.
[02:25] Miguel: good. also retention  how long are traces and request logs stored? we have regulatory windows.
[02:30] Jesse: retention is configurable per org: default 30 days for traces, 90 days for request logs in hosted; Dedicated/private you can set retention or route to your S3/GCS. we also support export hooks for long term archival.
[02:45] [03:05] Jesse: back to debugging flows  i'll recreate the failing request flow. here's the error on the trace: 'model OOM' then a fallback. you can see the routing policy triggered a fallback to a lower-capacity model variant. the console shows the rollout policy and the fallback reason.
[03:25] Laura: oh the fallback is exactly what we saw in prod. can we detect regressions like quality changes after a model rollout?
[03:30] Samir: yes, Console integrates with Redwood Optimize evals  you can attach prompt sets to a rollout and see quality diffs. also alerts can be set on model-level metric regressions.
[03:40] Miguel: are there SLO alerts from tracing? we want to hook into our pager.
[03:44] Jesse: traces generate latency histograms and error rates per route, you can export metrics to Prometheus or Cloud Monitoring. alerts can be pushed to PagerDuty/Slack.
[03:55] [04:10] Laura: the request logs view  do you keep headers? we need to make sure auth tokens are unaudited.
[04:15] Jesse: headers are stored but we mask Authorization by default. you can configure additional masking rules. for compliance we also have audit logs that record who accessed which trace/log; RBAC controls limit access by role.
[04:30] Priya: on RBAC  can we tie into SSO / SAML? we require SCIM provisioning.
[04:35] Samir: yes SSO with SAML and SCIM user provisioning are supported for Dedicated and Hosted enterprise tiers; we also have granular RBAC roles. we'll attach the SSO/SCIM setup doc.
[04:50] [05:05] Miguel: when you say 'trace id' vs 'request id'  are they the same? we correlate across systems.
[05:10] Jesse: good callout. internally we use a trace_id for spans and a request_id for HTTP request. Redwood's console correlates them; trace detail shows both and we emit correlation ids to your logs so you can join in Splunk/BigQuery. sometimes the export shows 'traceId' vs 'trace-id' depending on source  small naming mismatches happen.
[05:30] Laura: ok, show us an example of a customer debugging a timeout end-to-end.
[05:35] Jesse: yes  example: trace shows repeated 504s at the network boundary. expanding the spans shows the router retrying then a model server returning a timeout. clicking 'request logs' we see request headers and the middleware log 'latency=1200ms'. from there you can use the console to open the raw request and download a HAR if needed.
[05:55] [06:20] Jesse: i'm going to open the request logs filter  here's a search query we use: route: /generate AND status: >=500 AND model: redwood-7b-quant. it returns the requests and you can group by user_id.
[06:35] Miguel: does the console support live tailing of logs during an incident?
[06:40] Jesse: yes, there's a live tail UI and you can attach a trace to the tail. for high-volume tails we recommend sampling and then using our export to raw storage for deep dives.
[06:55] [07:10] Laura: sampling  what about bias? we need to make sure sampling doesn't hide production errors.
[07:15] Samir: sampling is configurable by route and error state. you can set to always sample error responses, and sample non-error traffic at lower rates so you still keep representative data.
[07:30] [08:00] Jesse: switching to error analysis page  it surfaces top error types and affected routes. here's a common view where 'rate limit exceeded' appears because of a bad client retry. you can drill into a stack of request logs and the traces that hit the limit.
[08:20] Priya: do you preserve PII for debug? again, we have PHI concerns.
[08:25] Jesse: by default we apply PII redaction patterns; with Dedicated/Private you can run the sanitization in your VPC so logs never leave your network unencrypted. we'll include a diagram in follow-up.
[08:40] [09:05] Ethan: high level question  if we go Dedicated can we use our own model variants and still get the same console telemetry?
[09:10] Samir: yes, Dedicated supports self-hosted model variants with our runtime. telemetry, traces and logs are collected by the same agents. there might be small differences in span naming if you alter telemetry SDKs, but correlation keys are maintained.
[09:30] [10:00] Jesse: demo note: sometimes our auto-transcribe mislabels spans or proper nouns in the Fireflies export, so when you download the transcript you'll see minor typos  unrelated to console behavior.
[10:15] Miguel: understood. can we set a retention policy that dumps logs over to our S3 bucket nightly?
[10:20] Jesse: yes export hooks support S3/GCS and you'll get gzipped ndjson for logs. exports can be scheduled nightly or triggered by thresholds.
[10:35] [11:05] Laura: let's talk about alerting on model quality regressions  can tracing help detect hallucinations?
[11:10] Samir: tracing alone doesn't detect hallucination, but combined with Optimize's evals and the request logs you can run evals on sampled outputs and trigger alerts when semantic metrics drop. we also have a feature to attach expected output patterns per route.
[11:30] [12:00] Jesse: i want to show a quick walk-through of a debugging flow we ran with another customer  we had an API key misconfiguration that caused 401s, tracing showed auth failure at the ingress, request logs showed missing Authorization header, and audit logs showed config change from a service account. that saved about 2 hours.
[12:20] Priya: good example. audit logs  where are they stored and who can access them?
[12:25] Samir: audit logs are immutable and stored with your account; access is controlled via RBAC. for Dedicated you can ship audit logs to your SIEM.
[12:40] [13:15] Miguel: are the request payloads indexed? i.e., can i run full-text search across payloads?
[13:20] Jesse: payloads are indexed with configurable fields. full-text search is supported but we recommend indexing only necessary fields to control cost and PII.
[13:35] [14:00] Laura: ok, switching to perf  how do we run the benchmark you recommended for token throughput?
[14:05] Jesse: we can run a 1-day benchmark from Redwood Dedicated pool against your sample workload. we provision a dedicated job that simulates your traffic pattern including sequence lengths and concurrency. we produce a report showing p95 latency, token-per-second, and cost estimate.
[14:25] Ethan: what's needed to start that?
[14:28] Samir: we'll need sample prompts, expected concurrency, and a representative dataset. Miguel can share a small set of traces and request ids for seeding.
[14:40] Miguel: i'll extract some tomorrow.
[14:42] [15:00] Jesse: quick note on sampling and KV cache: if you use prefix caching the trace spans will show cache hits vs misses. sometimes span labels differ per runtime, e.g., 'kv-cache' vs 'kv_cache', so search queries should account for variants.
[15:20] [16:00] Laura: are request logs encrypted at rest?
[16:05] Jesse: yes encrypted at rest. Hosted uses provider-managed keys by default; Dedicated and Private can use your KMS. we also support envelope encryption for extra layer.
[16:20] Priya: do you keep raw user inputs in logs in Hosted? we might need to scrub inputs.
[16:25] Samir: inputs are stored unless you enable input redaction or streaming-only mode. we recommend streaming-only for highly sensitive data so no payloads are persisted.
[16:40] [17:10] Jesse: i'm going to show request log export. clicking export yields an ndjson file with each line a JSON request record. you can choose to exclude certain fields. note, sometimes our CSV export flattens nested metadata which can introduce key naming changes.
[17:30] Laura: any rate limiting on exports?
[17:33] Jesse: exports are rate-limited per org to protect the console; for larger dumps we recommend direct S3 exports.
[17:45] [18:05] Miguel: what's the SLA for Dedicated telemetry? we need low loss and high availability.
[18:10] Samir: Dedicated telemetry has an SLA; we can include specifics in the SOW. typically >99.9% ingestion uptime depending on commit level.
[18:25] [19:00] Jesse: demo interruption  quick question from chat: 'does request logs show model logits?' short answer: no, logits are not exposed in hosted telemetry, you can enable additional debug outputs in dedicated runtime but that's gated.
[19:20] Priya: can debug outputs be restricted to a VPC?
[19:25] Samir: yes gated debug outputs for Dedicated only and behind admin controls.
[19:40] [20:05] Jesse: jumping to a live incident playback  here's a recorded trace from last week where a routing policy misconfiguration sent traffic to a slow variant. you can replay request payloads to a sandbox model to reproduce.
[20:25] Laura: the replay feature  can it hit a non-production model?
[20:28] Jesse: yes you select a target model version/variant for replay; replays are isolated and never write back to production systems.
[20:40] [21:00] Miguel: how long does it take to provision sandbox for replay?
[21:05] Jesse: usually a few minutes for an already-provisioned sandbox, up to 30 minutes for cold start.
[21:20] [22:00] Ethan: for Dedicated, what's the onboarding timeline?
[22:05] Samir: typical Dedicated onboarding is 4-6 weeks after contract, includes infra provisioning, VPC peering, KMS setup and a runbook handoff. Private on-prem can be 8-12 weeks.
[22:25] [23:00] Jesse: security note  we are SOC2 Type II compliant for Hosted enterprise. we can share the report under NDA.
[23:12] Priya: please do. we will need SOC2, ISO and network diagrams.
[23:18] Samir: will do  adding to action items.
[23:30] [24:05] Laura: are there per-route quotas shown in the console?
[24:10] Jesse: yes per-route rate and token quotas are visible and you can set hard limits. rate limit events appear in error analysis.
[24:25] Miguel: for debugging, can we correlate CPU/GPU metrics with traces?
[24:30] Jesse: yes, we surface serving node metrics and you can click through to the infra view which links to GPU utilization and memory OOMs. we also export metrics to Prometheus for historical analysis.
[24:50] [25:20] Laura: okay let's recap and next steps.
[25:25] Samir: recap: 1) Jesse will provision a sandbox console and share sample traces + request logs; 2) Samir will send pricing and pilot SOW; 3) Atlas to share sample traffic and failing request ids for the 1-day benchmark; 4) Redwood to share SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs.
[25:45] Ethan: that covers most items. one more compliance question  do you support data residency in EU for hosted?
[25:52] Samir: yes we have EU regions and can pin data residency for hosted accounts. for stricter needs Dedicated/Private are recommended.
[26:05] [26:30] Priya: timeline for the benchmark results?
[26:35] Samir: after we get samples, the 1-day benchmark report is produced within 3 business days.
[26:45] Miguel: we'll try to get samples tomorrow.
[27:00] [28:00] Jesse: final demo note  sometimes transcription exports show speaker labels like 'Speaker 2' instead of names. that's just the meeting tool, console telemetry is unaffected.
[28:20] Laura: thanks that's helpful.
[28:25] [29:00] Samir: any blockers to moving forward with sandbox and benchmark?
[29:05] Ethan: no blockers but need internal sign-off from security which may take a week.
[29:10] Priya: i'll coordinate.
[29:20] [30:00] Jesse: ok provisioning notes  i'll send the sandbox invite and a quick runbook for using the request logs and trace correlation.
[30:15] [31:00] Samir: i'll include pricing scenarios for hosted vs dedicated plus a pilot SOW with timelines. i'll also attach the SOC2 NDA link.
[31:20] Miguel: one more micro question  when a model fallback happens does the console surface both responses?
[31:25] Jesse: yes it surfaces the primary and fallback responses along with which routing policy kicked in, and you can diff outputs in the UI.
[31:45] [32:30] Laura: perfect. any other questions?
[32:35] Ethan: none from me.
[32:40] Priya: no.
[32:42] Samir: great, we'll follow up with the items discussed. thanks everyone for your time.
[32:50] --- End of meeting ---
